entities.summary:
Świętochłowice is an industrial city in Upper Silesia, southern Poland, within the Katowice conurbation and today’s Metropolis GZM. Situated on the Silesian Highlands along the Rawa drainage, it grew from medieval agrarian settlement into a nineteenth- and twentieth-century coal and metalworking centre under Prussian and then Polish sovereignty.

Its modern identity is bound to Upper Silesia’s borderland history—Germanisation and Polonisation struggles, interwar autonomy politics, wartime occupation, and postwar socialist industrialisation. Dense housing and heavy industry made it typical of the polycentric Silesian urban region.

Today it remains a compact city with powiat rights whose story is inseparable from the wider Katowice agglomeration’s economic transformations.
